processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: The best of what has been heard concerning a man who has intercourse with a slave-girl in whom he has a share is that the hadd punishment is not carried out on him, the child is attributed to him, and the slave-girl is valued at the time she became pregnant, so he gives his partners their shares of the price, and the slave-girl becomes his. This is the practice among us. Malik said about a man who permits another man to have intercourse with his slave-girl: If the one to whom she was permitted has intercourse with her, she is valued on the day he had intercourse with her, whether she became pregnant or not, and the hadd is averted from him by that. If she becomes pregnant, the child is attributed to him. Malik said about a man who has intercourse with his son's or daughter's slave-girl: The hadd is averted from him, and the slave-girl is valued against him, whether she became pregnant or not.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to a man who went on a journey with his wife's slave-girl and had intercourse with her, and his wife became jealous and mentioned that to Umar ibn al-Khattab, so he asked him about it. processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman that she said: Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, went out to Makkah, and with her were two female slaves of hers and a young slave belonging to the sons of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq. She sent with the two female slaves a striped cloak over which a green cloth had been sewn. The young slave took the cloak, ripped it open, extracted it, put felt or fur in its place, and sewed it up. When the two female slaves arrived in Madinah, they handed it over to his family. When they opened it, they found the felt inside and did not find the cloak. They spoke to the two women, and they spoke to Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, or wrote to her. They accused the slave. The slave was questioned about it and confessed. Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, ordered that his hand be cut off. Aisha said: 'The cutting is for a quarter dinar and more.'

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Nafi' that a slave of Abdullah ibn Umar stole while he was a runaway. Abdullah ibn Umar sent him to Sa'id ibn al-As, who was the governor of Madinah, to cut off his hand. Sa'id refused to cut off his hand and said: 'The hand of a runaway thief is not cut when he steals.' Abdullah ibn Umar said to him: 'In which Book of Allah did you find this?' Then Abdullah ibn Umar ordered that his hand be cut off.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Zurayq ibn Hakim that he informed him that he caught a runaway slave who had stolen. He said: His matter was difficult for me. He said: So I wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asking him about it, and he was the governor at that time. He said: I informed him that I used to hear that when a runaway slave steals while he is a runaway, his hand is not cut. He said: So Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to me in reply to my letter, saying: 'You wrote to me that you used to hear that when a runaway slave steals, his hand is not cut. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book: 'As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they earned, an exemplary punishment from Allah. And Allah is Mighty, Wise.' [Quran 5:38] So if his theft reaches a quarter dinar or more, then cut off his hand.'

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik reported that it reached him that al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Salim ibn Abdullah, and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr used to say: 'When a runaway slave steals what requires cutting, he is cut.' Malik said: This is the matter about which there is no disagreement among us: that when a runaway slave steals what requires cutting, he is cut.

processed_hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، /27 أَنَّ /26 الْقَاسِمَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ /26 ، /26 وَسَالِمَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ /26 ، /26 وَعُرْوَةَ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ /26 ، كَانُوا يَقُولُونَ : /20 " إِذَا سَرَقَ الْعَبْدُ الْآبِقُ مَا يَجِبُ فِيهِ الْقَطْعُ ، قُطِعَ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَذَلِكَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي لَا اخْتِلَافَ فِيهِ عِنْدَنَا ، أَنَّ الْعَبْدَ الْآبِقَ إِذَا سَرَقَ مَا يَجِبُ فِيهِ الْقَطْعُ ، قُطِعَ /10 *

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Ibn Shihab, from Safwan ibn Abdullah ibn Safwan, that Safwan ibn Umayyah was told: 'Whoever does not migrate will perish.' So Safwan ibn Umayyah came to Madinah and slept in the mosque using his cloak as a pillow. A thief came and took his cloak. Safwan caught the thief and brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: 'Did you steal this man's cloak?' He said: Yes. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that his hand be cut off. Safwan said to him: I did not intend this, O Messenger of Allah. It is charity for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Why not before you brought him to me?'
